intended_object: A canonical bijection between two of the library's own encodings of the degree-one finite places of the rational function field C(X). One encoding uses height-one primes of C[X]; the other uses the library's generic place model for finite extensions, applied to C(X) over itself. Inferred from the docstring and the body.
explanation: The definition restricts `ratFuncFinitePlaceEquivFiniteExtension` to the degree-one subtypes. That equivalence comes from `heightOneSpectrumEquivOfAlgEquiv` along the algebra isomorphism between C[X] and the integral-closure chart. The restriction uses `Equiv.subtypeEquiv`, with a lemma saying that place degrees agree under this map. This is transport glue between two internal models of the same set of places, used for the library's averaging arguments. It is not a mathematical notion with its own literature definition. Mathematically both sides are the set of rational finite points of the affine line, so the equivalence is just bookkeeping, and there is nothing to compare with a textbook object.
